summary: Biologist-facing reporting generally separates technical failure from morphology warnings and correctly limits the pilot results to sampled ROIs and one specimen per group. However, the active production profile automatically re-watersheds every successfully splittable U-Net component whose centerline exceeds 20 um, including a smooth synthetic object, and the U-Net-primary tuner explicitly penalizes the fraction above 20 um. These rules can fragment or tune away a genuine long-nucleus phenotype before warning-only classification, so the claim that plausible mutant morphology remains measurable without morphology-directed acceptance or tuning is not supported.

findings.title: Enabled 20-um splitter can fragment genuine long nuclei solely because of length
findings.impact: A genuine mutant long-nucleus phenotype can be converted into several apparently ordinary nuclei before morphology warnings and specimen-level summaries are produced. Pixel coverage is preserved, but biological object identity, count, length distribution, and tracking population are changed, directly contradicting the claimed morphology-neutral production semantics.
evidence: production_profiles/saturn_v5_7_1_model_c_epoch003.json:74-77 enables the splitter in the reviewed production profile.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:2813-2842 proposes and accepts partitions for every component above the trigger based only on child minimum lengths and shortening relative to the parent.

tests/test_saturn_v57_unet_primary.py:301-322 demonstrates automatic multi-label partitioning of a smooth uniform elongated component and asserts that all resulting measurements are no longer above 20 um.

V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:23-27 claims a smooth >20 um object remains visible with a review warning, which is only true when the splitter fails or is disabled and is not guaranteed by the active profile.
findings.recommendation: Require objective fusion evidence before splitting, such as multiple core-head predictions or a validated probability valley, and preserve the unsplit parent measurement and identity as explicit provenance. Add adversarial tests showing that smooth straight, smooth curved, wide, thin, and mutant-like long single nuclei remain one technical-valid instance under the production profile.

findings.title: U-Net-primary tuning objective penalizes long morphology
findings.impact: Parameter selection is explicitly driven away from candidates producing objects over 20 um. Even without a WT label, this encodes an expected morphology and can suppress a genotype-dependent long tail, conflicting with the claim that comparative tuning does not reward WT-like length or use morphology as a tuning target.
evidence: utils/tune_parameters_Saturnv5_7_1.py:661-680 adds very_long_frac*1000 to unet_primary_score.
utils/tune_parameters_Saturnv5_7_1.py:683-689 selects unet_primary_score when TUNING_OBJECTIVE is unet_primary.
utils/tune_parameters_Saturnv5_7_1.py:802 activates that objective for U-Net-primary evaluation.
tests/test_tuner_v57.py:235-283 verifies that a 21-unit object receives at least a 1000-point penalty compared with a 9-unit object.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:18-19 says comparative tuning does not reward similarity to wild-type length, which is incompatible with the active length-tail penalty.
findings.recommendation: Remove morphology-frequency penalties from comparative U-Net-primary selection, or justify a technical failure metric using independently annotated fused-component truth that does not treat length alone as impossible. Add a test asserting equal comparative scores for otherwise identical smooth plausible objects below and above 20 um.

findings.title: Broad phenotype-preservation claim lacks targeted thin and fragmentation evidence
findings.impact: The available tests cover many warning categories but do not establish that thin genuine nuclei are retained or that fragmented-looking detections avoid biologically consequential over-counting. Automated success cannot substitute for mask-level biological validation of these cases.
evidence: tests/test_saturn_v571_audit_blockers.py:24-92 covers smooth-long and branched-long examples.

tests/test_saturn_v57_multisample.py:test_comparative_morphology_warnings_remain_technical_valid covers warning retention but starts from already constructed track rows rather than segmentation masks.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:35-79 reports only one KJ and one WT specimen and does not identify independently annotated manual masks for the required morphology case set.
findings.recommendation: Create a blinded, manually masked morphology challenge set with independent specimens containing short, long, wide, thin, curved, fragmented-looking, fused-looking, single-slice, and low-ratio examples. Report instance recall, split/merge errors, and specimen-level sensitivity with and without each technical threshold.

limitations: Focused tests could not be executed because the repository-local .venv interpreter was absent and the available Python installation lacked pytest; command results were '.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe is not recognized' and 'No module named pytest'. Conclusions therefore rely on direct source, profile, test-definition, and generated-report inspection.
Per instruction, no full image stack was run and other reviewers' outputs were not read.
The two-specimen replay artifacts cited by V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md were treated as implementation evidence, not as independent biological ground truth.
No manual instance masks, independent specimen series, or external biological validation were available to determine whether >20 um components are truly fused or genuine long nuclei.
recommended_follow_up: Disable the length-only overlong splitter and long-tail tuner penalty for the acceptance candidate, or supersede this audit with independently validated fusion evidence and morphology-neutral rules.

Add production-profile integration tests using smooth and curved >20 um single objects, true multi-core fusions, thin objects, and fragmented-looking neighbors; assert identity preservation as well as foreground coverage.
Validate segmentation and tracking against blinded manual masks from multiple independent WT and mutant specimens before drawing biological conclusions.
Continue reporting repeated-ROI exposure strictly as sampled ROI volume and retain the explicit one-specimen-per-group non-inference language.
